messages:
Evan: Quick sync idea  push canonical precision candidates + safety metadata into the model manifest (so compiler/runtime share one source of truth). Pros/cons?
Priya: I like the single contract. Concern: customers need per-tenant SLA overrides. How do we safely expose that?
Evan: Manifest would include allowed_bitwidths, degradation_budget, and an allowed_overrides predicate. Runtime accepts overrides but must validate they are subsets and that estimated degradation <= manifest.degradation_budget.
Sam: Operationally we also need cheap smoke signals baked into manifests: quality_anchor (tiny vector), latency_delta_estimate, token_cost_delta so canaries can quickly surface regressions.
Lina: FP8 still trips on long-tail prompts. We need token-level degscore telemetry and an "early-fallback" policy: if degscore crosses threshold within first N tokens, escalate to safer precision and optionally regenerate last K tokens.
Priya: Regeneration during streaming breaks many clients. Suggest alternative: soft-fix emit a corrective append or provide a regenerate flag that clients can opt into. Document tradeoffs in RFC.
Sam: For Dedicated/Private, manifests must be signed and versioned. Add migration playbook: manifest pinning, staged canaries, forced rollback hooks. Also include validation_artifact_hash to tie CI results to the manifest.
Evan: Minimal manifest sketch we should include in RFC (as text): precision_candidates, degradation_budget, allowed_overrides, confidence_thresholds, fallback_policy_id, quality_anchor_hash, latency_delta_estimate, cost_delta_estimate, validation_artifact_hash, manifest_version, signature.
Lina: Runtime implications: compiler can pick kernels deterministically when it reads precision_candidates + headwise_flags, but runtime still needs to negotiate per-request (tenant overrides/SLA). We must design override-validation checkpoints: pre-exec validate, canary-acceptance, post-exec telemetry check.
Priya: UX: customer override flow should show expected delta estimates and whether the override is allowed. If override rejected, runtime should return a clear error code and suggested alternatives.
Sam: Edge-case: what if a later manifest tightens degradation_budget mid-flight? We need a deprecation window and migration policy so existing in-flight sessions aren't abruptly changed.
Evan: Action items: Evan  draft RFC with manifest schema + sample rollout plan. Priya  mock customer-override UX + error codes. Sam  signing/versioning + migration checklist for Dedicated/Private. Lina  sketch telemetry hooks for token-level degscore and early-fallback smoke checks.
sig-bot: RFC created: /rfc/manifest-precision-contract-v1  reviewers: Evan, Priya, Sam, Lina
